title: Apply the guarded ordinary manual serving-revision switch

gates.command: docker compose run --rm --no-deps backend python -m mypy src/face_moment

gates.name: Serving-revision switch tests
gates.command: docker compose run --rm backend python -m pytest tests/serving_control/test_serving_revision_switch.py

verify.summary: Compacted retained final functional PASS. Current task status is done.
Compacted final lifecycle closure: current task status is done.

evidence_required: FT-002-AC-001 RED: serving_control has no ordinary manual A-to-B command that first invokes processing-owned target-B validation and, only for validated B, separately consumes the completed read-only exact-A guard inside the shared serving context before committing B; GREEN: the owner command returns the audited requested/committed revision result, rejects invalid, unknown or ineligible B before commit with A and every Photo/processing/deployment/model-process snapshot unchanged, rejects a validated B when the separate guard blocks with the same unchanged snapshot, and commits B only after validated B plus a clear guard; decisive comparison: disposable target-validation, blocked-guard and clear-guard cases compare the two processing-boundary calls, committed revision and before/after side-effect snapshot, while an interleaved admission/switch yields only committed A plus rejected B or committed B plus a B admission; artifact: focused serving-control integration output and transaction trace.
purpose: Implement the serving_control-owned manual command that invokes processing target-B validation, separately applies the completed processing guard, and serializes a possible A-to-B serving decision with admission.
success_outcome: A manual A-to-B request returns its audited owner result, rejects invalid, unknown or ineligible B before commit and a validated B when the completed guard blocks with A and all side-effect projections unchanged, and commits B only through the serial serving context that admission also uses after both accepted processing results permit it.
anti_goals: Do not reimplement the processing guard or read/write processing rows directly from serving_control.
Do not add a revision registry, switch/job lifecycle, persisted mode, automatic drain, rollback, deployment action or generic coordination framework.
Do not add a transport route, staff role, authentication mechanism, realtime query behavior, Calibration integration or FT-011 model-comparison execution.

forbidden_scope: The processing-owned exact-A guard and its state-matrix proof owned by TASK-039-T2-FT-002-W6
Realtime reference-query execution and participant result assembly owned by FT-004
Calibration calculation, recommendation, comparison execution and run persistence owned by FT-011
Photo delete, restore and hard-purge behavior owned by FT-012
Model asset deployment, worker/realtime restart, automatic rollback or direct database edits as an ordinary revision-switch path
stop_conditions: Admission and the serving decision cannot serialize through the accepted serving context without a new ownership edge or durable coordination mechanism.
A correct command requires serving_control to inspect processing rows directly, processing to mutate serving selection, or a new switch lifecycle/state.
A correct command would require a new public transport/auth contract, model comparison integration or deployment behavior.

constraints: Inside the owner-held serving context, serving_control resolves exact current A, first calls processing-owned target-B validation, and only for a validated B separately calls the completed processing-owned read-only exact-A guard; neither accepted processing boundary is replaced by the other, and the owner returns the contract result naming requested and committed revisions.

Admission obtains the same serving-context serialization before it commits its immutable revision snapshot and matching pending state, so it either completes under A before the guard or starts under B after B commits.

Use one disposable SPA with known current validated A, a validated B plus invalid, unknown and ineligible B candidates, and task-owned Photos only for command integration; the fixture has known initial state, safe rerun and complete cleanup, retains the existing caller authorization boundary and adds no transport or role.
invariants: A target-validation rejection or guard rejection preserves A, every Photo and processing state, and the current deployment/model-process binding.
Only a processing-validated B plus a clear separately invoked completed guard permits B commit; serving_control never accesses processing rows directly and processing never writes serving selection.
The command introduces no persisted switch state, background drain, automatic rollback or deployment side effect, and model comparison remains test-only with no bypass.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-001: A disposable target-B validation integration proves serving_control calls processing to validate the requested B: invalid, unknown and ineligible B each reject before commit with the audited requested/current result, unchanged A, and no Photo, processing, deployment or model-process side effect; this is command-owned validation proof, not deployment/runtime-admission proof.

With a separately validated B, disposable blocked and clear guard integrations prove serving_control separately invokes the completed read-only exact-A guard, preserves A and the same no-side-effect snapshot on a blocker, and commits B only on a clear result without adopting TASK-039's five-state exact-A matrix claim.

An interleaved admission/switch transaction probe proves one serial outcome only: completed A admission blocks B, or B commits before the new Photo receives its immutable B snapshot and matching B pending row.

Static and transaction tracing proves the two accepted serving_control -> processing calls are target-B validation and the separate read-only exact-A guard, with no direct processing-row access or foreign write bypass; model-comparison fixtures cannot invoke or bypass the command.
